title: Cap. VIII Arg.: God is rich in mercy — therefore he reprobates only from foresight of demerits
pass_a_gloss: God is rich in mercy: But if he were to reprobate certain ones from his mere will, and not on account of foresighted sin, in such an act nothing of mercy would appear: Therefore he reprobates from foresight of demerits, or from the foresighted evil use of free will about to last unto the end.
pass_b_english: Argument: God is rich in mercy. But if he reprobated some from his mere will and not for foresighted sin, nothing of mercy would appear in that act. Therefore he reprobates from foresight of demerits — or from foresighted evil use of free will lasting to the end.
source_text: Deus est dives in misericordia: Sed si aliquos reprobaret ex mera sua voluntate, et non propter praevisum peccatum, in tali actu nihil misericordiae appareret: Ergo reprobat ex praevisione demeritorum, sive ex praeviso malo usu liberi arbitrii ad finem usque duraturo.
